credential_kind: Entra federated identity credential (FIC, workload identity)
typical_lifetime: no secret material to expire (federated trust only); FIC trust config itself has no expiry
rotation: rotate by updating the FIC's issuer/subject binding; no secret value to rotate
revocation: delete the FIC on the app registration; immediate
audit: Entra sign-in logs show the federated token exchange

typical_lifetime: recommended max 180 days per Microsoft guidance
rotation: manual or automated re-upload before expiry; overlapping validity windows avoid downtime
revocation: delete/disable the certificate on the app registration; immediate
audit: Entra sign-in + audit logs record credential add/remove
storage: PFX/PEM on disk or a certificate store; never argv/env

typical_lifetime: 365 days default; up to 400 days max (feature-flagged, GitLab 17.6)
rotation: "rotate" issues a new token with same scope and deactivates the original, immediately
revocation: revoke invalidates immediately; both actions irreversible
storage: GitLab-side only (opaque token value held by the user); GitLab recommends CI/CD job tokens instead of a PAT for CI/CD pipelines

typical_lifetime: same 365-day default / 400-day max as PAT; set at project or group level
rotation: same rotate semantics as PAT but scoped to the project/group
storage: attached to the project/group, not a personal account

rotation: none needed; a fresh token is minted per job
revocation: expires automatically at job end; scope limited to configured allowed projects
audit: GitLab pipeline logs + job token allowlist audit
storage: never stored; injected as job-scoped env for the job's own duration

credential_kind: GitLab CI `id_tokens` (OIDC JWT for external secrets)
typical_lifetime: single job execution; `aud` claim scoped per job
rotation: none; minted fresh per job run
audit: GitLab pipeline logs; consumer (Vault/Key Vault) logs the exchange
storage: not stored; exchanged directly for a downstream credential (Vault JWT auth, Azure federated credential)

typical_lifetime: configurable, e.g. `secret_id_ttl=10m`; also bounded by `secret_id_num_uses` (e.g. 40 uses)
rotation: Pull mode (Vault generates the SecretID) preferred over Push mode in most cases; batch tokens recommended with AppRole
revocation: bounded by secret_id_ttl and secret_id_num_uses; explicit revocation not described on the AppRole page
audit: not described on the AppRole page
storage: not described on the AppRole page (RoleID is a low-sensitivity selector; SecretID is the secret)

typical_lifetime: default 1 hour TTL / 24 hour max TTL (adjustable per role)
rotation: Vault mints a new unique credential per request; static roles support scheduled password rotation instead
revocation: Vault's internal lease-revocation system invalidates the DB user at lease expiry or on explicit revoke
audit: unique credentials per service let questionable data access be traced to the service instance by SQL username
storage: not described on the database secrets engine page

typical_lifetime: not stated in the Key Vault overview
rotation: not stated in the Key Vault overview
revocation: not stated in the Key Vault overview
audit: vault logging can be archived to a storage account, streamed to an event hub, or sent to Azure Monitor logs
storage: Key Vault itself (Standard: FIPS 140 L1 software; Premium: FIPS 140-3 L3 HSM)

credential_kind: Claude Code login credential (OAuth session / API key)
typical_lifetime: session-scoped; Claude Code's own token lifetime (not separately published in fetched pages)
rotation: re-authenticate with /login (a startup warning appears 3 days before a login expires); `apiKeyHelper` re-run on a 5-minute default TTL (`CLAUDE_CODE_API_KEY_HELPER_TTL_MS`)
revocation: /logout (for a Console sign-in it removes and revokes the credential that sign-in wrote)
audit: not separately published in fetched pages
storage: macOS Keychain (falls back to ~/.claude/.credentials.json mode 0600 if the Keychain write fails); Linux ~/.claude/.credentials.json mode 0600; Windows %USERPROFILE%\.claude\.credentials.json with user-profile ACL

credential_kind: Claude Code MCP server OAuth token
typical_lifetime: per MCP server's own OAuth token lifetime (server-defined)
rotation: refreshed automatically by Claude Code; re-authenticate from /mcp when the server rejects the refresh token
revocation: Clear authentication in /mcp, claude mcp logout <name>, or claude mcp remove (also deletes stored tokens and client registration); or revoked by the MCP server
audit: not separately published in fetched pages
storage: "stored securely" (location of the tokens not named on the page); OAuth sign-ins stored per endpoint; a pre-configured client secret goes to the system keychain (macOS) or a credentials file, not the config

typical_lifetime: not stated in S1297 beyond the token response fields (expires_in); see auth/token-lifetimes-cae.md
rotation: a new downstream token is requested by an OBO exchange of the user access token; the response can also carry a refresh token
storage: middle-tier tokens must not be sent anywhere except their intended audience
